title: What India's Slower Manufacturing Growth Tells Us
description: India's Manufacturing PMI, a key economic report, showed slower growth in July 2026. It dropped to 53.9 from 54.5 in June, indicating expansion but at a softe.

faq.q: What is considered a "good" Manufacturing PMI reading?
faq.a: Generally, any reading above 50 indicates expansion, which is positive. A consistently high reading (e.g., in the mid-50s or higher) suggests robust growth. However, a very high reading might also sometimes signal overheating and potential inflationary pressures.

faq.q: Who conducts the Manufacturing PMI survey in India?
faq.a: The HSBC India Manufacturing PMI is compiled by S&P Global from responses to questionnaires sent to purchasing managers.

faq.q: How often is the Manufacturing PMI released?
faq.a: The Manufacturing PMI is released monthly, typically at the beginning of the month, providing a timely update on the previous month's activity.

faq.q: Does the Manufacturing PMI affect the stock market?
faq.a: Yes, it can. Investors and analysts watch the PMI closely as it provides early insights into economic trends. A stronger-than-expected PMI can be seen positively, while a weaker one might lead to some caution, but it's just one of many factors influencing the market.

faq.q: What is the difference between Manufacturing PMI and Services PMI?
faq.a: Manufacturing PMI focuses on companies that produce physical goods (like factories). Services PMI (also compiled by S&P Global) focuses on industries that provide services (like finance, healthcare, hospitality). Both track similar metrics but are tailored to their respective sectors. There's also a Composite PMI which combines both.
